packages.title: The full-width offline card fills its width
packages.commit: Commits: the round's changes to `src/styles/global.css` (only the rules named here, none of the other session's lines) and the tester's additions to `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts` are this run's.
brief: WEB-709 (R2F-1, S1) is a regression of round 2. WP35 (WEB-705) moved the offline card from span 6 to span 12, so above 800 px it is a band about 1180 px wide with three short lines at its left (`.feature-offline p { max-width: 26rem }`) and roughly two-thirds of it blank. It reads as an unfinished card. WP35's acceptance measured only vertical slack, so it passed. Seen in `artifacts/ux-web/home.en.desktop.light.full.png`, screen 3.

Fix it with CSS only, no new content, markup or strings. The markup stays as it is (`src/components/HomePage.tsx:135-141`: `.feature-icon` span, `h3`, `p`). Keep WP35's grid as it is: offline stays span 12, and the calendar, voice and details rules don't change.

Above 800 px, lay the card out in two columns, with the icon and heading on the left and the paragraph on the right. In the base rules (`global.css:670-676`), make it: `.feature-offline { grid-column: span 12; background: var(--soft); display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1.4fr); column-gap: 32px; align-items: start; }`, `.feature-offline .feature-icon { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; justify-self: start; }`, `.feature-offline h3 { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 2; }` and `.feature-offline p { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1 / span 2; margin-top: 0; max-width: 32rem; }`. The paragraph's top lines up with the icon's top. The `h3` keeps its 18 px top margin from `.feature-card h3`.

In the `@media (max-width: 800px)` block, extend the existing `.feature-offline { grid-column: span 12; }` (`global.css:1057-1059`) with `display: block;`, and add `.feature-offline p { margin-top: 10px; max-width: 26rem; }`, so that at 800 px and below the card is exactly what it is today: icon, heading and then paragraph, stacked. The 580 px and 360 px blocks need no change, because they inherit the 800 px rule.

Organizer's call: the reports gave two fixes, and this brief takes the reviewer's main one. The smaller alternative (only raise `.feature-offline p` to `max-width: 40rem`) would still leave about 40–45% of the band blank on the right. Use it only if the two-column layout clips or overflows in a render (for example at desktop-text200), and say so in your notes.

Then look at the renders at desktop 1440 (light and dark), at desktop-text200 and desktop-zoom200, and at a width between 801 and 1100 px, in EN, ES and CA. ES and CA headings run longer, so check that the heading wraps inside column 1 and nothing is clipped, because `.feature-card` has `overflow: hidden`.

Don't touch the other feature cards, the calendar drawing (WEB-706), the copy, the FAQ or anything outside `#features`. WP35 reported that between 801 and 1100 px, and at 200% text, the calendar card ends with some mint space below its drawing (9–19% of the card, under the 25% bound). That's accepted, so leave it as it is.
acceptance: On /, /es/ and /ca/ at 1440 × 1000, in light and dark: inside the offline card (`#features .feature-offline`), the paragraph sits to the right of the heading. The paragraph's left edge is at least 40% of the card's width from the card's left edge, and the paragraph's top is above the heading's bottom. The icon and the heading start at the card's left padding.

On / at 1440 × 1000, in light and dark, WP35's grid check still passes: the calendar spans two rows beside voice over details, offline spans the full width below them, and for the voice, details and offline cards the space between the bottom of the last child and the card's bottom edge is at most 25% of the card's height.

On /, /es/ and /ca/ at 1440 × 1000 with 200% text, and at 1000 px wide: no text in the offline card is clipped (the card's `scrollWidth` and `scrollHeight` don't exceed its `clientWidth` and `clientHeight`), and the heading and paragraph don't overlap.

On /, /es/ and /ca/ at 390 × 664: the offline card is display block, and its icon, heading and paragraph are stacked in that order (each one's top is at or below the bottom of the one before). The paragraph has a 10 px top margin and a computed max-width of 26rem (416 px), as before this round.

Visual (verifier, from the render `home.en.desktop.light.full.png` and its dark twin, screen 3): no more than about half the offline card's width is blank. No home scrolls sideways at 320 px. axe reports no violations on the three homes, light and dark. `npm run check` and `npm test` pass.

escalated.reason: Failed twice. The part of WEB-2 that WP15 and WP34 carry, the bare `/` routing and redirect, is escalated. Round 1, WP15: the routes and the 307 to /es/ and /ca/ worked, but the cache check failed because Next 16 overwrites Vary on the 200. Round 2, WP34: the check was relaxed (every answer for / is `private, no-store` and nosniff, and only the 307s carry `Vary: Accept-Language, Cookie`), and it passes locally (`tests/ux-web-global.spec.ts:91-136`). The briefed host-free redirect was not done: `src/proxy.ts:37` is still `NextResponse.redirect(new URL(homePath(language), request.url), 307)`. The evidence conflicts. The implementer says the built server already answers with a path-only Location even with a foreign Host header, but the tester found the Location absolute. Behind Cloud Run (`Dockerfile:18`, `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0`, `PORT=8080`), the edge worker rewrites a Location only when it starts exactly with `env.ORIGIN` (`edge/worker.ts:78-83`). So after a deploy, Spanish and Catalan visitors who type the bare address could be sent to the run.app host or to a dead host. This risk is inferred, not seen, and its cause is likely server-side. Recommendation: allow the one-line change at `src/proxy.ts:37`, `new NextResponse(null, { status: 307, headers: { Location: homePath(language) } })`, keeping lines 38-39 (`ux-web-global.spec.ts:127` already accepts a path-only Location). Then confirm with `curl -sI -H 'Accept-Language: es' http://localhost:3000/` and, after a deploy, on taskflow.garbar.tech. `src/proxy.ts` stays held until WP20 commits. WEB-2's other parts (WP20, WP22–WP24, WP28, WP29) stay planned.
